pool.text: Spanish conquest established Quito as the oldest capital in South America
Quito officially declared a city by colonial authorities
Granted the title "Muy Noble y Muy Leal Ciudad"
Became seat of a Real Audiencia of Spain
Quito briefly proclaimed de facto independence during the Quito Revolt
Movement launched to win independence from Spanish rule
Battle of Pichincha secured independence under Sucre and Bolívar
Four Days' War erupted across the nation
Quito declared first World Cultural Heritage Site by UNESCO
Minor eruption produced ash and smoke over Quito
Volcano Reventador erupted, showering city with several centimeters of ash
Construction of Metrobus (Ecovia) bus lines across Quito began
Municipality divided Quito into 32 urban parishes
Museo de Sitio La Florida opened to preserve archaeological artifacts
Municipality launched Bici Q bicycle‑sharing system
Virgin of Panecillo statue inaugurated on April 27
U.S. State Department notes pickpocketing as most common tourist crime
Quito Metro subway line opened for public service
Presidential candidate Fernando Villavicencio assassinated after Quito rally
Landslide broke water pipe, causing crisis for 400,000 residents
